messages:
Maya: Heads up — noticed the GPU-hours forecast is undercounting EU-west for the past 48h. Dashboard p99 shows a sharp drop but cluster metrics disagree. Passing to infra to triage. :thinking_face:
Sam: Saw that too. Looks like a labeling change from the node upgrade yesterday. Some nodes started reporting instance_label=`pool-v2` instead of `instance_pool`. Our aggregator group_by is `instance_pool` so those hours got dropped from the forecast dataset.
Liam: Ugh. That rename was rolled by the k8s ops job (k8s-label-sync) to standardize labels. We missed the backwards-compat mapping in the usage ETL.
Anika: Quick question — are we sure they were dropped and not double-counted? Could be a de-dup bug when label is present and also fallback tag exists.
Sam: Checked raw usage logs (node heartbeats + pod GPU attach) — the records are there with the new key, but the forecast-ingest job only looks for `instance_pool`. So they're excluded from the group-by which feeds the forecasting model. Not duplicated.
Cory: posting snippet of the problematic SQL we run in ingest: ```
SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) as hr, instance_pool, sum(gpu_seconds) as gpu_sec
FROM usage_raw
WHERE ts >= '{{start}}' AND ts < '{{end}}'
GROUP BY hr, instance_pool;
```
Cory: Since instance_pool is NULL for pool-v2 nodes, they show up as a NULL bucket and our downstream filter drops NULLs.
Maya: Can we do a fast fix by changing the ETL to coalesce both keys? Something like `coalesce(instance_pool, instance_label) as instance_pool` so we keep continuity?
Liam: That's the minimal change. We should also add a transformation to normalize older logs: map `pool-v2` -> `pool-v2` (same) but map any historical weird names too.
Anika: Agree. Also we need to update the metric definition doc and the Grafana panel query — right now the forecast dashboard filters instance_pool != NULL. That will keep showing the dip until we backfill.
infra-bot: Deploy job queued: jobs/etl-forecasting/patch-coalesce-labels (dry-run). CI checks ok.
Sam: Two parallel work items: 1) deploy coalesce change to ingest (low-risk). 2) schedule backfill for last 72 hours to recompute aggregates into the forecast materialized table.
Maya: Backfill considerations: we should avoid recomputing >7 days during business hours because it adds table scan pressure. Let's run the backfill off-peak and throttle the job. Also incrementally apply to only rows where instance_pool IS NULL.
Cory: Proposed backfill SQL: ```
INSERT INTO forecast_aggregates (hr, instance_pool, gpu_sec)
SELECT hr, coalesce(instance_pool, instance_label) as instance_pool, sum(gpu_seconds)
FROM usage_raw
WHERE ts >= '{{backfill_start}}' AND ts < '{{backfill_end}}' AND (instance_pool IS NULL OR instance_pool = '')
GROUP BY hr, coalesce(instance_pool, instance_label)
ON CONFLICT (hr, instance_pool) DO UPDATE SET gpu_sec = EXCLUDED.gpu_sec;
```
Liam: Ops note — ON CONFLICT update will replace whatever forecast_aggregates currently has. Good for correctness but will briefly change downstream inflight jobs that read aggregates. We should coordinate a maintenance window or mark the aggregates as "updating" via a flag table.
Anika: For immediate alerting: modify the forecast alert rule to also fire on sudden drop in raw node GPU attach rate, not only aggregates. That will reduce time-to-detect similar label skews in future.
ops-oncall: I can run the backfill after midnight UTC. Suggest throttling concurrency to 4 and target 6-hour windows to minimize IO.
Maya: Great. Sam — can you own the ingest patch and the dashboard query update? Liam — can you run the backfill tonight with ops-oncall? Cory — please prepare the SQL and a short rollback plan. Anika — please update the metric spec doc (docs/metric-defs/usage.md) with the coalesce change and add a note about label migration.
Sam: On it. I'll push the ingest patch to canary in 10m and watch CPU/RDS IO. infra-bot pinged the canary channel when done.
infra-bot: Canary deployment complete: etl-forecasting v2.1.3-canary — healthy.
Maya: After canary green, let's run a 12h quick recompute on a test partition to ensure numbers match expected. We should also run a diff job: `SELECT hr, instance_pool, old.gpu_sec, new.gpu_sec FROM old_agg old JOIN new_agg new USING (hr, instance_pool) WHERE abs(old.gpu_sec - new.gpu_sec) > 0.05 * old.gpu_sec;`
Cory: I'll prepare the diff script and a short report with top 10 instance_pools by absolute delta.
Sam: Canary looks fine. Rolling to prod in 5.
Liam: Ops-oncall and I will kick off the backfill at 00:30 UTC, 6-hour chunks, concurrency 4, expected finish ~04:30 UTC. We'll post progress in this thread.
ops-oncall: Backfill started. First chunk done, slight RDS IO spike but within threshold.
Maya: Noted — once backfill finishes, we'll re-run the forecast model and re-publish capacity projections. I expect usage + GPU-hours to rise ~3-6% in EU-west for the next weekly forecast. Update cost projection runbook accordingly.
Sam: Prod deploy done. No errors.
ops-oncall: Backfill complete. Diff report: 137 hr-instance_pool rows corrected, EU-west +4.2% GPU_hours over the 72h window. Report uploaded: https://redwood/internal/reports/gpu-label-backfill/1925123456
Maya: Thanks team. Follow-ups: (1) Add a migration checklist for label renames. (2) Add an automated test in ingest CI that rejects schema changes unless a coalesce or mapping exists. (3) Add an alert for large NULL buckets in the aggregator.
Anika: I'll add the metric doc changes and create the CI test PR.
Cory: I'll file a retro ticket to improve our label-change playbook.
Maya: Closing thread once PRs are merged and the dashboard shows corrected numbers. :white_check_mark:
Sam: PRs opened: etl coalesce patch + grafana panel tweak + metric-doc update. Marking this thread resolved from my side.
Liam: Thanks all.
